title: Singing with no microphone in the big Dreamland
summary: She started songs in the middle of the huge floor and the band picked them up; she and Ollie Powers had the biggest voices and never strained.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: But tell me, in those days now, of course you didn't have microphones.
No, no such thing as a microphone.
So it must have been hard sometimes --

Well, I'll tell you what. I'd be out there on the floor singing. And like if I finished this song, somebody would say to me, 'Alberta, sing so and so and so,' I would start it out in the middle of the floor in Dreamland -- and you don't know how big Dreamland was, do you. It was almost a block square, Dreamland was. And I would start the song and
Lily and them would pick it up. From me just starting it, and go right on with me. And play it. I don't know.
But could Lily, for instance, from the stage could she hear you?

They must have heard me. I'd just hum it. You know, didn't have a microphone, so I'd say -- (singing) "kind treatment will make me love you." and they'd pick it up from there. And they'd go right on and play the song, you know. When I'd get through, I'd throw up my hand.
But then I would imagine, you know, you had a lot of people in there.
Lot of noise.
There would be a lot of noise?
Oh, lot of noise. But they played it just the same, and never missed a note, and neither would I.
But wouldn't you have to sing a little bit extra loud, more than you would --
Well, I had a big voice.
Kind of a strain, wasn't it?
It wasn't then, for some reason. I don't know why.
What about an orchestra coming -- then it must be pretty hard --
It was a whole orchestra.
It was?

Yeah. The whole orchestra. And they played with just the same -- I don't know, when I'd start, they'd go on with me, and when I'd finish up I'd throw up my hand and they'd stop. And if I wanted to start a song -- not only me, but the rest of the singers, they'd start, I'd start -- they'd start a song, why they'd pick it up and go right on. But I think Ollie Powers and I had the biggest voices, so the rest of them mostly used to have to go up close to them so they could hear them.
Never used megaphones in those days?
No, uh-uh. Even when I went over USO I didn't use no microphone.
No?
No. I got a whole lot in those books there saying I didn't use microphones.
I was wondering, you know, in a theater, for instance, where you have the big pit band in front of you, how could you, as a singer, be heard? You've got the band playing there and --
I don't know. I'd be heard. Yeah, uh-huh. I don't know how I did it. It wasn't a strain at the time. Uh-uh.
You told me once that you never strained.
Never. I never strained. And as I say,

now, well none of us used a microphone, only the ones with the little small voices, like Bertha. She had a sweet little voice. They had to listen for her, and pick up for her, you know. But Ollie Powers and me, we --
You didn't have a microphone --

No, uh-uh. But they'd have to start close, you know, so they could -- we'd stand -- Ollie and I'd just stand in the middle of the floor, way back in the back, and start our songs, and they'd go from there.
